column7: Review finding against #2700's own fix in the same branch, never on main. #2700 correctly replaced markWebAuthnCredentialClonedDisabled's full-row GORM Save (whose 0-rows upsert fallback re-INSERTED a hard-deleted passkey) with a column-scoped conditional UPDATE, and in doing so added early returns on !matched and on err != nil that sat BEFORE the EventWebAuthnCloneDetected audit write. The Save it replaced always reached that write, so a signature-counter regression stopped leaving any audit trail at all whenever the credential was deleted -- or the database briefly failed -- in the window between the assertion check and the disable. rejectIfCloned discards this function's error, so the failure mode was pure silence with a successful-looking login refusal. The regression was also covered by a comment claiming rejectIfCloned already audits the clone signal for the credential-missing case; it does not -- that else branch fires only on a failed LOOKUP, never on a lookup that succeeded and an UPDATE that then matched nothing. Fixed by writing the clone-detected audit UNCONDITIONALLY before any branch can return, with what happened to the row in the detail (disabled / already deleted / could NOT be disabled, treat as unmitigated). Deliberately NOT split into a second webauthn.error event: the clone verdict was already reached before this function was called, so there is exactly one incident, and a second event would let incident counts double -- the mfa.error/mfa.failed split exists for the opposite case where no verdict was reached. Both subtests assert the EFFECT (an audit row exists, with a detail that does not claim a mitigation that did not happen) because no return value in the chain distinguishes audited from silently skipped. The deleted-credential subtest reproduces the real interleaving against a real database -- a store wrapper returns the genuine row from the lookup and hard-deletes it, so the following UPDATE matches zero rows -- and drives the full rejectIfCloned path, so the discarded error is inside the subject. Red-proven by reinstating #2700's early returns: both subtests go red with ZERO audit events
